subject: confidence bands for logistic regression when data is fraction of success

messages.author: 9e66ac6517e290b7
messages.subject: confidence bands for logistic regression when data is fraction of success
parts:
I already asked this on stackoverflow (http://stackoverflow.com/questions/32464641/confidence-intervals-for-logistic-fit-in-seaborn) but after trying some more it seems that the explanation may be with ggplot2. My original data has fractions of of successes for specific values of X:

(x1: y11, y12, y13)
(x2: y21, y22, y23)
(x3: y31, y32, y33)
....

where yij is the fraction of successes in session j for xi.

and I am using ggplot with logistic regression to plot the data. And the issue is the confidence band displayed by ggplot does not match that calculated using glm. I followed this post: https://groups.google.com/d/msg/ggplot2/Ls5U0_SrCJE/5tpqTNPNFAAJ to obtain the confidence band:

> library("MASS")
> data(menarche)
> predd = cbind(menarche, predict(logr_m, menarche, type="link", se.fit=T))
> ggplot(predd, aes(x=Age, y=Menarche/Total))+stat_smooth(method="glm", family="binomial" ) + geom_line(aes(y=binomial()$linkinv(fit)),data=predd,colour="red",linetype=2) +  geom_line(aes(y=binomial()$linkinv(fit + (1.96*se.fit)))) + geom_line(aes(y=binomial()$linkinv(fit - (1.96*se.fit))))
Warning message:
In eval(expr, envir, enclos) : non-integer #successes in a binomial glm!
>

and get the plot attached. However when I convert the data to generate dummy binary responses, ggplot confidence interval matches that computed from glm. Now my questions are:

1) Given the warning from ggplot, what is the right way to plot and fit this kind of data?
2) What does the confidence band for logistic regression mean when ggplot is provided with fraction of successes ? It does not seem to be the link inverse of the confidence interval in the linear fit.
